# ADR NNNN — <Decision in the imperative> (ADS-xxx)

- Status: Proposed | Accepted | Accepted — implemented | Partially implemented | Superseded by ADR NNNN | Rejected
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Scope: the files, packages, or systems this binds
- Linear: ADS-xxx
- Supersedes / Superseded by: ADR NNNN (or —)

## Context

The forces. What is true today, what pressure prompted a decision, what constraints are fixed.
No solution language.

## Decision

What we will do, in the active voice. Concrete enough that a reviewer can tell whether a PR
complies. State what is explicitly _out_ of scope.

## Consequences

### Positive

### Negative / accepted costs

### Follow-on work

What this obliges us to build or revisit later, with ticket links.

## Alternatives considered

One paragraph each, and why not. A rejected option with a reason is the most reused part
of an ADR.

## Compliance

How a reviewer or CI check verifies conformance (lint rule, script, test, or "manual review").
